value_domain: Capital gains on active shares and units, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 2
variable_description: Gains on shares or trust units used in the taxpayer's business, worked out by indexing the cost base rather than discounting the gain. Indexation is only open to old holdings: the ATO restricts the method to "capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999". The active label is a claim about eligibility rather than about the asset, because a gain belongs on the active side only where the entity is going on to claim the small business 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption or the roll-over.
value_definition: A dollar amount before any capital losses, the CGT discount or the small business concessions are applied, being one of three method cells on the shares and units row of the schedule used up to 2012-13.
limitation: The column thins mechanically as pre-September 1999 holdings are sold down, so a fall over the 2000s is a cohort effect rather than a change in investor behaviour. It is also not ordinary share trading: only gains for which small business concessions are being claimed reach the active side at all.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, shares and units, indexation method cell of the current year capital gains grid, which is a defined cell of the older CGT schedule. The ATO instructions define the three calculation methods, the acquisition date test for indexation and the rule that decides whether a gain is active.
evidence_quote: indexation method (see note 2 of the worksheet) for capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what indexation is or why the active split exists.

value_domain: Capital gains on active shares and units, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 4
variable_description: Gains on business shares or trust units held at least a year, before the discount has been taken. The ATO opens the discount method to "assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you're not using the indexation method" and notes it "does not apply to companies", so a company lodging this schedule leaves the cell empty. The discount is applied several steps later, after capital losses, so the figure here is a gross gain. Its presence on the active side also signals that a small business concession is being claimed on the same gain.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses and gross of the discount percentage, being one of three method cells on the shares and units row of the schedule used up to 2012-13.
limitation: It cannot be halved to get a taxable gain, because losses are applied before the discount and the small business concessions after it. A zero for a company is a feature of the tax law rather than evidence that the company sold no long-held shares.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, shares and units, discount method cell of the current year capital gains grid on the older CGT schedule. The ATO instructions define the holding period test, exclude companies from the discount and set out where in the sequence the discount is applied.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is undiscounted or that companies cannot use the method.

value_domain: Capital gains on active shares and units, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1
variable_description: Gains on business shares or units that qualify for neither indexation nor the discount, usually because they were held under a year. The ATO puts the method last in the order: the other method applies "if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies". Read against the discount cell on the same row, this figure is a rough measure of short-held disposals inside a small business. Nothing is reduced later, so the amount enters the net capital gain calculation at full value.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses and of the small business concessions, carrying no later reduction for the CGT discount, being one of three method cells on the shares and units row.
limitation: It is not purely short-term trading, because a company that cannot use the discount reports its long-held share gains here as well. The row also cannot separate listed shares from unlisted units, a distinction the redesigned schedule later drew.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, shares and units, other capital gains cell of the older CGT schedule grid. The ATO instructions define the other method as the residual of the three and set out the order in which losses are best applied against the methods.
evidence_quote: 'other' method (if neither the indexation method nor the discount method applies)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the other method is or why the cell is not simply short-term trading.

value_domain: Capital gains on active real estate, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 2
variable_description: Gains on business property bought before 21 September 1999, worked out by indexing the cost base. Where both indexation and the discount were available the taxpayer had to pick one, and the ATO warns that at the point of choosing, the worksheet figures "don't yet reflect any capital losses or CGT discount you may be able to apply", so the split between this cell and the discount cell beside it records a judgement made without the full picture. Property is the usual active asset, which makes this row the busiest part of the active side.
value_definition: A dollar amount before losses, the discount and the small business concessions, being one of three method cells on the real estate row of the schedule used up to 2012-13.
limitation: It says nothing about which property was sold or where it was: a farm, a shop and a factory produce one figure. The amount is a gain rather than a sale price, so it cannot be used to value business property or to track property markets.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, real estate, indexation method cell of the older CGT schedule grid. The ATO instructions define indexation, state when a taxpayer must choose between indexation and the discount, and describe what the choice is made on.
evidence_quote: Where you can use both the indexation method and the discount method for an asset, you must choose which method to apply.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the method split reflects a taxpayer choice.

value_domain: Capital gains on active real estate, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 2
variable_description: Gains on business premises held at least twelve months, before the discount is taken, and the main doorway into the small business concessions. The ATO only asks for the active split when concessions are in play: "You'll only need to differentiate your capital gains between active and non-active assets if you're going to apply the small business concessions." A figure here therefore identifies a taxpayer claiming the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption or the roll-over on a property gain, not merely someone who sold a building.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses, of the CGT discount and of the small business concessions, being one of three method cells on the real estate row.
limitation: A gain that qualified for the small business 15-year exemption is missing entirely, because the ATO directs those amounts to a separate item of the schedule rather than into this grid, so the column understates concession-eligible property sales. Main residences never appear at all.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, real estate, discount method cell of the older CGT schedule grid. The ATO instructions state when the active split has to be made, list the three concessions that qualify a gain for the active side and direct 15-year exemption gains elsewhere.
evidence_quote: You'll only need to differentiate your capital gains between active and non-active assets if you're going to apply the small business concessions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a value here is a concession claim rather than a property sale.

value_domain: Capital gains on active real estate, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 2
variable_description: Gains on business property that fell outside both indexation and the discount, typically sold within a year of purchase. A dollar here costs more tax than a dollar in the discount cell beside it, because nothing is halved later, which is why the ATO advises that a taxpayer usually gets the greatest benefit by reducing gains calculated using the other method first, then indexation, then discount. Company disposals also land here whatever the holding period, since companies cannot use the discount.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses and of the small business concessions, entering the calculation at full value with no later discount, being one of three method cells on the real estate row.
limitation: A large figure is not proof of speculative flipping, since a company's sale of long-held premises reports here too. Development profits taxed as ordinary business income never reach the CGT schedule, so this is not a measure of property trading.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, real estate, other capital gains cell of the older CGT schedule grid. The ATO instructions define the other method as the residual, exclude companies from the discount and set out the loss ordering that makes this cell the first target for losses.
evidence_quote: Within the non-active and active categories, you usually get the greatest benefit by reducing: capital gains calculated using the 'other' method, then capital gains calculated using the indexation method, then capital gains calculated using the discount method.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said why this cell attracts capital losses first.

value_domain: Capital gains on other active assets, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 2
variable_description: Gains on business assets that are neither shares, units nor real estate, indexed rather than discounted. This is the catch-all row of the older grid: goodwill, licences, contractual rights and any CGT event that does not attach to a named asset class. Goodwill is the ATO's own illustration of an active asset, since "an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business)". Indexation confines the cell to assets acquired before 21 September 1999, so it empties out through the 2000s.
value_definition: A dollar amount before losses, discount and concessions, being one of three method cells on the other CGT assets and any other CGT events row of the schedule used up to 2012-13.
limitation: The row is defined by exclusion, so its composition shifts whenever a new named row is added to the form: forestry interests and hedging financial arrangements were later carved out of it. It also mixes asset disposals with CGT events in which no asset changes hands.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, other CGT assets and any other CGT events, indexation method cell of the older grid. The ATO instructions define an active asset with goodwill as the example, and give the acquisition date test that limits indexation.
evidence_quote: Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what falls into the catch-all row or that its content changed as rows were added.

value_domain: Capital gains on other active assets, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 2
variable_description: Gains on other business assets held at least twelve months, which in practice is mostly goodwill. When a business is sold as a going concern its largest gain usually lands here rather than on the real estate row, because goodwill is not land. The ATO requires the active side to carry only gains that qualify for one or more of the small business 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over, and directs any gain that does not to the non-active side. The discount is applied later in the schedule, so the figure is not halved.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses, discount and concessions, being one of three method cells on the other CGT assets and any other CGT events row.
limitation: It cannot be attributed to a particular asset, so a goodwill sale, a licence surrender and a payment for a restrictive covenant are indistinguishable. Whether an asset is active is a test the taxpayer applies to itself, so the boundary against the non-active row records a self-assessment the ATO may later disturb.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, other CGT assets and any other CGT events, discount method cell of the older grid. The ATO instructions state which concessions qualify a gain for the active side and where a gain goes when it does not qualify.
evidence_quote: If the asset doesn't qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the active boundary is a self-assessment.

value_domain: Capital gains on other active assets, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 2
variable_description: Gains on other business assets where neither indexation nor the discount applies, entering the calculation at full value. For this row the other method covers short-held rights and, importantly, every company gain, since companies cannot claim the discount. Because losses are worth most against undiscounted gains, this is normally the first cell a taxpayer applies capital losses to. The ATO also excludes losses on personal use assets from the row: "You disregard capital losses from personal use assets and you can't apply them to reduce capital gains."
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses and of the small business concessions, with no later discount, being one of three method cells on the other CGT assets and any other CGT events row.
limitation: A zero does not mean no business assets were sold, because the same disposal appears in the indexation or discount cell when the acquisition date or holding period allows. The cell also cannot be compared across entity types, since a company's whole capital gain sits here while an individual's is spread across the three methods.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, other CGT assets and any other CGT events, other capital gains cell of the older grid. The ATO instructions define the other method, exclude companies from the discount and state the treatment of personal use asset losses in this row.
evidence_quote: Don't include any capital loss made from personal use assets at Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the cell behaves differently for companies or that personal use asset losses are excluded.

value_domain: Capital gains on an active forestry managed investment scheme interest, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1; ATO, Trust tax return 2012 instructions, CGT schedule
variable_description: Gains on a forestry managed investment scheme interest held as a business asset, worked out by indexing the cost base. The cell is close to unused in practice, because indexation needs an asset acquired before 21 September 1999 and the forestry row was only added to the schedule after 2007. The PLIDA table carries the column for every year regardless, so an empty cell in an early year means the row did not exist on the form rather than that no forestry interest was sold.
value_definition: A dollar amount before losses, discount and concessions, being one of three method cells on the forestry managed investment scheme interest row of the schedule used up to 2012-13.
limitation: Emptiness here carries no information about forestry activity, because the combination of an old acquisition date and a late-arriving form row makes the cell almost impossible to populate. Money received for thinning is assessable income rather than a capital gain and never appears in this row.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, forestry managed investment scheme interest, indexation method cell of the older grid. The ATO's 2012 trust instructions confirm the forestry row belongs to that generation of the schedule, and the CGT schedule instructions give the acquisition date test that makes indexation almost unavailable for these interests. The claim that the column is carried for years before the row existed is read from the PLIDA table structure.
evidence_quote: a CGT event occurs in relation to a forestry managed investment scheme (FMIS) interest that is held other than as an initial participant
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the column exists in years before the form row did.

value_domain: Capital gains on an active forestry managed investment scheme interest, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains on a forestry interest held as a business asset for at least twelve months, before the discount is taken. The interest is a right in a plantation, and for a subsequent participant holding it on capital account the ATO treats money from selling the interest or receiving harvest proceeds as "capital proceeds for CGT purposes". Sitting on the active side means the taxpayer is claiming a small business concession as well as the discount, which is unusual for what is normally a passive investment.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses, discount and concessions, being one of three method cells on the forestry managed investment scheme interest row.
limitation: It cannot be read as forestry investment returns, because an initial participant, who deducts the cost of the interest, is taxed under a different regime and does not report here. Ongoing management fees are deductible rather than added to the cost base, so the gain is not a return on the investor's total outlay.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, forestry managed investment scheme interest, discount method cell of the older CGT schedule grid, and the ATO's capital gains guide sets out how a forestry interest is taxed on capital account, which decides what the amount comprises.
evidence_quote: Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a forestry interest is or how the initial and subsequent participant treatments differ.

value_domain: Capital gains on an active forestry managed investment scheme interest, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return 2012 instructions, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule
variable_description: Gains on a business forestry interest that qualify for neither indexation nor the discount, generally sold within a year. The forestry row has an unusual population behind it, because a CGT event on a forestry interest forces the schedule to be lodged whatever the size of the gain: the ATO requires it where "a CGT event occurs in relation to a forestry managed investment scheme (FMIS) interest that is held other than as an initial participant", outside the $10,000 test that governs everything else. Small forestry gains are therefore over-represented compared with small gains of any other kind.
value_definition: A dollar amount gross of losses and of the small business concessions, with no later discount, being one of three method cells on the forestry managed investment scheme interest row.
limitation: It cannot distinguish a sale of the interest from the receipt of harvest proceeds, which are both CGT events on the same asset. Nor does it say whether the taxpayer was an initial or a subsequent participant, which is the fact that decides the whole tax treatment.
rationale: The data item label names the active assets, forestry managed investment scheme interest, other capital gains cell of the older grid. The ATO's 2012 trust instructions give the forestry-specific lodgment trigger, which is what makes this row's population different from the rest of the schedule.
evidence_quote: a CGT event occurs in relation to a forestry managed investment scheme (FMIS) interest that is held other than as an initial participant
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that forestry events bypass the schedule's dollar threshold.

value_domain: ATO assessment identifier for the return the schedule was lodged with
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: Which assessment of the entity's return this schedule was captured against, rather than anything about the capital gains themselves. The ATO issues a notice of assessment when a return is processed and can revise it afterwards, since "this review period is normally 2 years, but in certain circumstances it can be 4 years", and each revision produces a further assessment. One entity and income year can therefore carry more than one assessment. Reading the field as an administrative version marker is the safe course: the ATO does not publish a definition of it as it appears in this asset.
value_definition: An administrative number attached to an assessment of one entity for one income year. It has no economic content and no published code list or format.
limitation: It cannot date anything, and it is not a count of amendments unless the numbering is sequential, which is nowhere published. Rows that differ only in this field may be successive assessments of the same return rather than separate lodgments, so counting rows overstates the number of schedules filed.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page defines this field for the capital gains tax tables, so the reading rests on what an ATO assessment is and on the field sitting beside the processed date and income year on the same row. The notice of assessment page supports the claim that a single income year can carry more than one assessment.
evidence_quote: Under the law, we have a period of time to review your tax return. During this time, we may increase or decrease the amount of tax payable or refundable on your initial NOA.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Assessment number' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to tell whether the column was data or administration.

value_domain: ABS BLADE business identifier
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The entity that lodged the capital gains tax schedule, keyed the way businesses are keyed in BLADE. The schedule is attached to a company, trust or superannuation fund income tax return, so this identifies an entity rather than a person; the synthetic person key on the same row is what links the record into the person-level asset. Because BLADE combines business activity statements, business income tax filings and payroll reporting, the key is what lets a capital gain be set against the same business's turnover, employment and survival. It appears on every year of the capital gains tables.
value_definition: An opaque business-level identifier, one value per business unit, stable across the yearly capital gains tables and across the other BLADE-linked business collections.
limitation: It is not an ABN and cannot be looked up. An entity that restructures may take a new key, so a run of schedules for what an owner would call one business can break in the middle. The key also does not say whether the lodger is a company, a trust or a fund, which the entity type column carries.
rationale: The capital gains tax collection is one of the ATO sources ABS lists as feeding BLADE, and the data item list gives this field as the business number on every capital gains table. The mapping of the field to the BLADE business unit is read from the table structure rather than from a published data dictionary.
evidence_quote: Australian Taxation Office: Business Activity Statements (BAS), Business Income Tax (BIT) filings, Pay as You Go (PAYG) summaries, Single Touch Payroll (STP), JobKeeper Payment Scheme, JobMaker Hiring Credit Scheme, Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and Consolidated Groups
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Business Number' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which asset the key belongs to or what it can be joined to.

value_domain: Capital gains from collectables, schedule used to 2012-13 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, What is a CGT asset?
variable_description: Capital gains for the year on paintings, jewellery, antiques, coins, rare books and stamps kept for personal enjoyment. The ATO's list is closed, and the class only enters the CGT net above a threshold: a gain or loss is disregarded where "you acquired the collectable for $500 or less". Losses are ring-fenced, since "you can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains (including future capital gains) from collectables", which is why the schedule gives collectables their own row and a separate carried-forward loss column. This is the collectables figure on the form used up to 2012-13.
value_definition: A dollar amount before losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions, sitting alongside the indexation, discount and other method cells that make up the collectables row of the older schedule.
limitation: Because the $500 acquisition threshold removes most items, the column measures the top of the collectables market rather than household ownership of art or jewellery. Collectables can never be active assets, so nothing here can reach the small business concessions.
rationale: The data item label names the collectables capital gains figure on the CGT schedule, and the ATO's capital gains guide defines what a collectable is, gives the acquisition threshold and states the loss ring-fencing that explains the separate row. The variable is confined to the tables covering 2000-01 to the first part of 2012-13, where the older form applied.
evidence_quote: You can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains (including future capital gains) from collectables.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Capital gains - Collectables' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what counts as a collectable or why they get a row of their own.

value_domain: Capital gains from collectables, redesigned schedule (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, step 1 and step 4
variable_description: Capital gains from collectables on the redesigned schedule, where they are one of nine named categories of current year gains. From 2012-13 item 1 of the schedule lists asset types rather than the active and non-active method grid the earlier tables carry, and the ATO tells the taxpayer to organise each worksheet under categories that "are the same as those set out in item 1 of the CGT schedule". A collectables gain received through a trust goes in the collectables row and not the trust row, and must be grossed up first. This is the same idea as the differently spelt column on the older tables, under a different form.
value_definition: A dollar amount for one entity and income year, gross of losses and of any discount, entered at the collectables label of item 1 and added into total current year capital gains.
limitation: It is not directly comparable with the older tables, which carried the collectables gain a second time split by method across cells this form does not have, so a series spanning 2012-13 is not continuous. A trust distribution entered here has been grossed up by two or four, so the amount can be several times what the trust actually paid out.
rationale: The data item label names the collectables label of item 1 on the redesigned CGT schedule, which the variable's table coverage from the second part of 2012-13 onwards confirms. The ATO instructions list the item 1 categories, place trust collectable gains in their own row and set out the grossing-up factors.
evidence_quote: If your entity was entitled to an amount of capital gain for a collectable from a trust, include the amount in row 8 of table 1
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Capital gains - Collectables' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it read identically to the older column it is not comparable with.

value_domain: Capital gains on listed shares, CGT schedule item 1 label A (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 1 label A
variable_description: Capital gains the lodging entity made in the year on shares in companies listed on an Australian securities exchange. It is the first of the nine asset-type rows the redesigned CGT schedule introduced for 2012-13, and it is entered gross: the ATO tells the lodger not to apply "capital losses", "the CGT discount" or "the small business CGT concessions" at this point. The matching loss row for the same asset class is label K.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross capital gain for one asset class, summed across the indexation, discount and other methods. Labels A to I add to label J, total current year capital gains.
limitation: The row does not record which calculation method produced the gain, so a listed parcel held more than twelve months cannot be separated from one held less. Listing status is the taxpayer's own classification of the asset at disposal, and no equivalent row exists before 2012-13, so a listed-share series cannot start earlier.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 1 label A of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions define the nine asset categories and state what is excluded from the amount.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at item 1 - labels A-I of the CGT schedule and write the total at label J Total current year capital gains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's label as its description, gave the value domain as not specified, and printed the sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Capital gains on unlisted shares, CGT schedule item 1 label B (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 1 label B
variable_description: Capital gains on shares not listed on an Australian securities exchange, mostly private company shares and shares on foreign exchanges. Read against label A on the same row it separates traded holdings from closely held ones, which is the split that matters for a business exit. The amount is gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross capital gain for one asset class, summed across the three calculation methods. It is one of the nine rows that add to label J.
limitation: Two very different disposals sit in the one figure: a foreign listed parcel and the sale of a family company. Nothing on the row identifies the company, so a gain here cannot be tied to the entity that was sold, and shares that qualified for the small business 15-year exemption are excluded from item 1 altogether.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 1 label B, Other shares, on the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions list the asset categories the lodger must organise gains under.
evidence_quote: These categories are the same as those set out in item 1 of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label as its description and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what 'other' excludes.

value_domain: Capital gains on listed trust units, CGT schedule item 1 label C (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 1 label C
variable_description: Capital gains on units in unit trusts listed on an Australian securities exchange, including listed property trusts and exchange traded funds. It records the disposal of the units themselves, not a distribution received from the trust; a distributed gain belongs at label G. The amount is gross of losses, discount and concessions.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross capital gain on listed units, entered before losses and the CGT discount. It is the third of the nine gain rows at item 1, and label M is its loss counterpart.
limitation: The row cannot be read as an exchange traded fund measure, because listed property and infrastructure trusts sit in the same box. It also says nothing about the underlying assets of the trust, so a gain here is a gain on the unit price rather than on any property the trust held.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 1 label C of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions distinguish that row from the trust distribution row.
evidence_quote: These categories are the same as those set out in item 1 of the CGT schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_domain: Capital gains on unlisted trust units, CGT schedule item 1 label D (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 1 label D
variable_description: Capital gains on units in unit trusts that are not listed on an Australian securities exchange, typically unlisted managed funds and private unit trusts. The gain arises when the units are redeemed or sold, so this is a disposal figure and not the trust's own realised gains passed through. Label G on the same row carries the distributed gain instead.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gross capital gain on unlisted units, reported without any split by calculation method. It is the fourth gain row at item 1, and label N is its loss counterpart.
limitation: A redemption from a managed fund and the sale of an interest in a family unit trust are indistinguishable here. Because unlisted units are often redeemed in parcels over several years, one year's figure is a poor guide to the size of the holding.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 1 label D of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions set out that the trust distribution amount goes at a separate row.

Paired with the total term at label B, it lets a reader place a row on the timeline of one contract without needing the sale date.
value_definition: A small whole number counting elapsed years within one arrangement, starting at 1. It is an ordinal position, not a calendar year.
limitation: It is not a date and cannot be read as one: 2 means the second year of the deal, not the year 2002. Treating consecutive rows as a clean sequence also fails where an entity has more than one earnout, since only one arrangement is reported on the schedule itself.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the question at item 7 label C of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions give a worked pairing of labels B and C.
evidence_quote: For example, if you're in the second year of a 4-year earnout arrangement, you would write: 4 at label B, 2 at label C.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's question as its description and a count inferred from the variable name, with a limitation saying only that the domain was inferred, so nothing ruled out reading it as a calendar year.

value_domain: Capital gain or loss under an earnout arrangement, CGT schedule item 7 label E (dollars, signed)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 7 label E
variable_description: The gain or the loss the entity made this year under an earnout deal, reported by the seller. Sign is carried by a flag rather than a minus: "If this amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label E." A buyer never completes it: the instructions send a buyer to the term questions only, and reserve this label for a seller.
value_definition: A dollar amount that may be either a gain or a loss, with the direction held in a separate loss indicator on the form rather than in the number itself.
limitation: Reading the column as a gain without the loss flag reverses the sign for some rows, and this dataset carries the amount without an obvious companion flag column. A loss under a look-through earnout may also have to be temporarily disregarded until future benefits are settled, so a zero can mean a deferred loss rather than no loss.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 7 label E of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions state the loss flag and the temporary disregard rule. The 2013 and 2025 forms show the wording change.
evidence_quote: Write at label E the amount of any capital gain or loss you made under your earnout arrangement in the income year for which this schedule is being completed. If this amount is a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label E.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so a signed amount was presented as an ordinary dollar column.

value_domain: Amended net capital gain or carried-forward loss, CGT schedule item 7 label G (dollars, signed)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 7 label G
variable_description: A corrected figure for an earlier year, lodged through this year's schedule because a look-through earnout payment changed what that year's gain should have been. The ATO instructs the lodger to "write at label G the amended net capital gain or capital losses carried forward amount resulting from the financial benefits received or provided", with the earlier year itself named at label F. The route exists only for look-through earnout rights created on or after 24 April 2015, which is why the column starts in the 2015-16 table.
value_definition: A dollar amount that replaces the earlier year's net capital gain, or its carried-forward loss where the L indicator is printed. It is a restatement of a past year, not a current year quantity.
limitation: The amount belongs to the year at label F, not to the year of the row it sits in, so treating it as current year activity misdates it. Access is also conditional: it is available only to individuals and to companies not acting as trustee, lodging on time and amending a single year, so most earnout corrections never appear here at all.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 7 label G of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions set out the conditions and the 24 April 2015 start date that match the column's first year table.
evidence_quote: write at label G the amended net capital gain or capital losses carried forward amount resulting from the financial benefits received or provided
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and a value domain inferred from the variable name, with a limitation that only said the domain was inferred, so nothing warned that the number restates a different income year.

value_domain: Capital gain previously deferred under transitional CGT relief, CGT schedule item 1 label S (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax schedule and instructions 2025 (QC 104724), item 1 label S
variable_description: A capital gain a superannuation fund parked in 2016-17 and is now bringing to account because the asset has finally been sold. The ATO explains the label as one that "recognises the previously deferred capital gain in an income year in which a realisation event occurs", and it exists only because funds were allowed to reset asset cost bases before the superannuation transfer balance cap took effect. The label first appears for 2017-18, and it is one of the few things that force a fund to lodge a CGT schedule regardless of the usual dollar threshold.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain deferred in an earlier year and recognised now, entered in the item 1 gains column alongside the asset-type rows.
limitation: The gain belongs economically to holdings built up over years before 2016-17, so treating it as a gain made in the reporting year overstates that year's activity. In the fplida registry the column is present only in the 2017-18, 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23 year tables, so a gap in the middle of the series reflects the data item list rather than a change to the form.
rationale: The PLIDA label is the wording of item 1 label S of the ATO capital gains tax schedule, and the instructions explain the transitional relief and the realisation event that triggers the entry.
evidence_quote: Label S on the CGT schedule recognises the previously deferred capital gain in an income year in which a realisation event occurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and a value domain inferred from the variable name, with a limitation that only said the domain was inferred, so nothing connected the column to the 2016-17 superannuation reforms.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method and Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units that the entity worked out by indexing the cost base, and on which it claimed no small business concession. Indexation is closed to anything bought after the 1999 change, the ATO restricting it to "capital gains made on CGT assets acquired before 11:45 am AEST on 21 September 1999". Non-active is the residual side of the grid: "If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is one cell of the part A grid on the old CGT schedule, whose rows are asset classes and whose three columns are the indexation, discount and other methods.
limitation: A zero here does not mean the entity held no shares. A gain on shares bought after September 1999 has to be reported in the discount or other column instead, so this cell tracks the age of the holding as much as the asset class. The old schedule also runs shares and units together and does not separate listed from unlisted, so it cannot measure exposure to the Australian market.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the three calculation methods and set the rule for what goes at non-active assets.
evidence_quote: If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what non-active means or which assets are allowed to use indexation.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units held at least twelve months, before the CGT discount is taken off. The ATO reserves the discount method for "assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method", and adds that "the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies". The amount is the whole gain, not the halved one, because the discount is applied later at part F.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Together with the indexation and other cells on the same row it makes up the entity's total share and unit gains for the year.
limitation: The figure overstates what is taxed, often by half, because the discount is applied two parts later on the same form. A non-trivial value on a company return is a reporting error rather than a discount claim, since a company is not entitled to the discount unless it is a life insurance company or a friendly society.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define when the discount method applies and which entities may use it.
evidence_quote: the discount method does not apply to companies, although it can apply to a limited number of capital gains made by life insurance companies
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said that the discount has not yet been applied.

value_domain: Shares and units capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Capital gains on shares and units that get neither indexation nor the discount, which in practice means parcels bought and sold inside twelve months. The ATO defines the calculation as follows: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds." Read against the discount cell on the same row, this column is a rough marker of short-held trading rather than long-term holding.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. Nothing further is deducted from these gains at parts F or G on the discount side, so the amount is closer to the taxable figure than its discount-method neighbour.
limitation: It is not a clean count of short-held disposals. A company reports every share gain here whatever the holding period, because it cannot use the discount, so the column measures entity type as much as trading behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active shares and units row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix sets out how the other method is worked out and when it must be used.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what the other method is.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Indexation method
variable_description: Capital gains on land and buildings worked out by indexing the cost base for inflation, where no small business concession is claimed. The ATO explains that the method "allows you to increase the cost base by applying an indexation factor (based on increases in the consumer price index up to September 1999)", and that "The indexation of the cost base of an asset is frozen on 30 September 1999." Because indexation stops there, a long-held property indexed in 2010 gets no relief for the eleven years since.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. The gain is measured against an indexed cost base rather than the historical cost, so it is smaller than the same disposal reported under the other method.
limitation: The old schedule has a single real estate row, so this cannot separate Australian property from foreign property; that split arrived only with the redesigned schedule, the 2013 form, which the CGT product picks up in the second part of 2012-13. Choosing indexation over the discount is an election, so a low value can reflect an adviser's arithmetic rather than the type of property sold.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix explains the indexation factor and the September 1999 freeze.
evidence_quote: The indexation of the cost base of an asset is frozen on 30 September 1999.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what indexation does to the cost base.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 1 calculation method
variable_description: Capital gains on land and buildings held at least twelve months, stated before the CGT discount, and outside the small business concessions. The ATO allows the discount method for "assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method". This is the cell where an investment property sale by a trust or a superannuation fund normally lands.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses. Cost base adjustments made before this point, such as capital works deductions claimed over the ownership period, are already inside the figure.
limitation: It is a gain, not a sale price, and one row covers every property the entity disposed of in the year, so it cannot count transactions or track a single property. Gains on a property owned by an individual do not appear in this dataset at all unless a CGT schedule was lodged.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the twelve-month test that puts a gain in this column.
evidence_quote: assets owned for at least 12 months and for which you are not using the indexation method
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is a gain before the discount.

value_domain: Real estate capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Capital gains on property that qualified for neither indexation nor the discount, which is mostly land and buildings bought and sold within a year. The ATO puts the calculation plainly: "To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds." Against the discount cell on the same row, a large figure here points to quick turnover or to a company vendor.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, and with no later reduction on the discount side of the form. It is the closest of the three real estate cells to a taxable amount.
limitation: Property developed and sold as a business is taxed as ordinary income, not as a capital gain, so the fastest turnover of all is missing from this column rather than concentrated in it. Nothing here says whether the property was residential or commercial.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active real estate row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix sets out the other method and when it must be used.
evidence_quote: You must use this method for any CGT assets, including shares or units, you have bought and sold within 12 months
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished this column from the discount one.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
variable_description: The residual row of the schedule under indexation: goodwill, contractual rights, payouts on the ending of an asset, anything without a row of its own. The ATO describes the class as covering a gain "that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule". Indexation confines it further to assets acquired before 11:45 am on 21 September 1999.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, measured against an indexed cost base. It is a catch-all row, so a single figure can combine several unrelated CGT events.
limitation: The column names no asset, so it cannot say what was disposed of, and two rows with the same amount can be entirely different transactions. It also absorbs whatever the form has not yet given a row to, which is why forestry and hedging gains sat here before those rows were added in 2008 and 2010.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix defines the residual category.
evidence_quote: Other CGT assets refers to the capital gain or capital loss that you have made and that doesn't fit into any of the more specific categories listed at item 1 of the CGT schedule
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is a residual class.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Other CGT assets and any other CGT events
variable_description: Gains on assets held twelve months or more that have no row of their own, reported before the CGT discount is applied. The ATO example of what this row absorbs is telling: it names "the disposal of your forestry interests in a forestry managed investment scheme or hedging financial arrangements". This is the largest and least specific of the non-active rows, and the one most likely to move when the form is redesigned.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It stands for a mixed bag of CGT events rather than one asset class.
limitation: The content of this cell is not stable across years. Forestry scheme interests were pulled out into their own row on the 2008 schedule and hedging financial arrangements on the 2010 schedule, so a level shift around those years is a change in the form rather than in behaviour.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix names forestry and hedging as examples of what falls in this class.
evidence_quote: the disposal of your forestry interests in a forestry managed investment scheme or hedging financial arrangements
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing warned that the row's coverage changed between editions of the form.

value_domain: Other CGT assets and events, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, 'Other' method
variable_description: Gains on unclassified CGT assets and events where neither indexation nor the discount applies, so the gain is simply proceeds less cost base. The ATO states the arithmetic as "you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds". For a company this is where most non-real-estate, non-share gains end up, because a company cannot use the discount column beside it.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no further method-based reduction. It combines any number of CGT events that share only their lack of a dedicated row.
limitation: This cell cannot be read as short-held activity the way the shares and real estate other-method cells can, because a company puts long-held assets here too. Payments that end a right or extinguish an asset also land here, and those are not disposals in any ordinary sense.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active other CGT assets row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO definitions appendix defines the other method.
evidence_quote: To calculate your capital gain using the 'other' method, you subtract your cost base from your capital proceeds.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained why a company concentrates in this column.

value_domain: Collectables capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, List of CGT assets and exemptions, Collectables
variable_description: Gains on art, jewellery, antiques, coins, rare books and stamps, worked out by indexing the cost base. The ATO lists the class as "artwork", "jewellery", "antiques", "coins or medallions", "rare folios, manuscripts or books" and "postage stamps or first day covers", and exempts an item entirely where "you acquired the collectable for $500 or less". Collectables get their own row because their losses are quarantined from every other gain on the schedule.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, measured against an indexed cost base. It sits with the discount and other-method collectables cells on the same row of part A.
limitation: The $500 exemption means the column only ever sees the upper end of the market, so it cannot describe household holdings of art or jewellery. A collectable held inside a superannuation fund is reported by the fund, so the column mixes personal collections with fund investments.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active collectables row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO page lists what counts as a collectable and the acquisition threshold below which no CGT arises.
evidence_quote: If you make a capital loss on a collectable you can only deduct it against capital gains from collectables, not from other capital gains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what a collectable is or why it has a separate row.

value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains on a forestry scheme interest worked out under indexation, a box that in practice is almost never used. The ATO treats a forestry interest as a CGT asset only for a later buyer: "You are a subsequent participant if you are not an initial participant", and "Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes". Indexation needs an acquisition before 21 September 1999, which is years before the forestry scheme rules and this row existed.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the indexation cell of the forestry row that the ATO added to part A of the schedule in the 2008 edition.
limitation: Expect this cell to be empty in almost every year, and treat a value in it as a lodgement error rather than a signal. The registry lists the column from 2000-01, but the 2007 edition of the schedule has no forestry row at all and the 2008 edition is the first that does.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the indexation column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide sets out when a forestry interest is held on capital account and produces a capital gain. That indexation is closed to assets acquired after September 1999 is my inference applied to this row, not a statement the ATO makes about it.
evidence_quote: Amounts you receive from a CGT event that happens to your forestry interest, for example the sale of your forestry interest or as harvest proceeds, are capital proceeds for CGT purposes
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the row postdates the years it is listed for.

value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains made by a later buyer of a forestry scheme interest held twelve months or more, before the CGT discount. The people who report here are second-hand holders, not the original investors: "In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant", and such buyers "are not able to claim a deduction for the costs of acquiring the forestry interest" and instead carry them in the cost base. The gain arises on sale of the interest or on receipt of harvest proceeds.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the discount cell of the forestry row, present on the schedule from the 2008 edition onwards.
limitation: The column describes the secondary market only. An initial participant deducts the cost of the interest and reports scheme income at the forestry income item on the return, so the money that built the plantations is not in this dataset. Thinning receipts are also excluded, being assessable income rather than capital proceeds.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines subsequent participants and their capital account treatment.
evidence_quote: In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said only later buyers report here.

value_domain: Forestry managed investment scheme interest capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Gains on a forestry scheme interest that qualify for no method relief, typically an interest bought and resold inside twelve months or held by a company. The ATO treats such an interest as a CGT asset only where it is not trading stock: "If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest." The gain here is simply proceeds less cost base.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no method-based reduction to come. It is the third cell of the forestry row, beside the indexation and discount cells.
limitation: This column cannot distinguish a quick resale from a company disposal, since both land here for different reasons. A dealer in forestry interests holds them on revenue account and reports nothing on this schedule at all, so the most active traders are invisible.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active forestry managed investment scheme row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide distinguishes revenue account from capital account holdings.
evidence_quote: If you hold your forestry interest on revenue account, there will be no CGT implications for the purchase and sale of your interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which holders are excluded.

value_domain: Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: Gains on a hedge that take capital character from the asset being hedged, reported under the discount method. The taxation of financial arrangements rules do this deliberately: they allow "gains and losses from certain hedging financial arrangements to be characterised and taxed in accordance with the tax treatment of the underlying item being hedged". Where the hedged item is a CGT asset, the ATO instructs the entity to "specify the amount of the gains or losses from the relevant hedging financial arrangements on the Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, undiscounted and gross of capital losses and the small business concessions. It is the discount cell of the hedging row, which the ATO added to part A of the schedule in the 2010 edition.
limitation: Only an entity with a valid hedging tax-timing election reports here, so the column measures an election as much as a hedging position; the same derivative held without the election produces ordinary income and never reaches this schedule. The registry lists the column back to 2000-01, but the 2009 edition of the schedule has no hedging row.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active hedging financial arrangements row of the discount column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO page explains how the TOFA hedging method gives a hedge the character of the hedged item and directs the amount to this schedule.
evidence_quote: gains and losses from certain hedging financial arrangements to be characterised and taxed in accordance with the tax treatment of the underlying item being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing connected the row to the TOFA hedging election.

value_domain: Hedging financial arrangement capital gains, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2016, Hedging financial arrangements
variable_description: Capital gains on hedging arrangements where no method relief applies, which is the usual cell for a company running a hedge book. The ATO explains that under a valid election "gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged". The old schedule gives the hedging row only these two boxes, discount and other; there is no indexation box.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, gross of capital losses and the small business concessions, with no later method-based reduction. It is the second and last cell of the hedging row.
limitation: The figure is one side of a hedge and means little on its own: the loss on the hedged asset it was meant to offset is reported in a different row of the same part, and the two cannot be paired from the schedule. It also gives no information about the notional value or the instrument type.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active hedging financial arrangements row of the other capital gains column in part A of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO page explains the character-matching rule that puts a hedging gain on this schedule.
evidence_quote: gains or losses from a hedging financial arrangement used to hedge against risks associated with a CGT asset will be treated as a capital gain or capital loss on the same basis as the capital gain or capital loss on the underlying CGT asset that is being hedged
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is one leg of a hedge.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 2B Applying prior year net capital losses
variable_description: Losses carried forward from earlier years and used up this year against gains worked out under indexation. The ATO defines the pool as follows: "Prior year net capital losses are the unapplied net capital losses carried forward from earlier income years." Deduction is compulsory once there is a gain to absorb them, and the losses must be used oldest first: "you must deduct them in the order in which they were made".
value_definition: A dollar amount of stored losses consumed in the year, not the stock of losses held. It is applied after current year losses and before the CGT discount and the small business concessions.
limitation: The column records losses spent, so it says nothing about losses remaining; the unapplied balance sits in the carried-forward columns of part I instead. A company only reaches this step if it satisfies the continuity of ownership or business continuity tests, so a zero can mean losses were forfeited rather than never made.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior year net capital losses applied row of the indexation column in part D of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define prior year net capital losses and the compulsory ordering.
evidence_quote: Prior year net capital losses are the unapplied net capital losses carried forward from earlier income years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing distinguished losses used from losses held.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 2B Applying prior year net capital losses
variable_description: Carried-forward losses applied against gains that will later be halved by the CGT discount. This is normally the worst place to put a loss, and the ATO says so, advising that entities "usually get the greatest benefit by reducing" other-method gains first, then indexation gains, then discount gains. A large figure here therefore usually means the entity had no cheaper gains left to absorb the losses.
value_definition: A dollar amount of losses from earlier years consumed against discount-method gains in this year. Because the discount has not yet been applied at this step, one dollar of loss here removes one dollar of pre-discount gain, worth only fifty cents of assessable gain.
limitation: The split between this column and its indexation and other-method neighbours reflects a placement choice made by the entity or its adviser, so it measures tax planning rather than the source of the losses. It also cannot be netted against the discount at part F, which is calculated after this step.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior year net capital losses applied row of the discount column in part D of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions describe the ordering that makes this the least valuable column to use.
evidence_quote: you usually get the greatest benefit by reducing: capital gains calculated using the 'other' method, then capital gains calculated using the indexation method, then capital gains calculated using the discount method
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said why the split across the three columns matters.

value_domain: Prior year net capital losses applied, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 2B Applying prior year net capital losses
variable_description: Carried-forward losses applied against gains that receive no discount and no indexation, which is where a well-advised entity puts them first. Each dollar applied here removes a full dollar of assessable gain. The ATO gives the entity the choice, saying prior year losses may be deducted "from any remaining capital gains in the way that produces the best result", subject only to using the oldest losses first.
value_definition: A dollar amount of losses from earlier years used against other-method gains in this year. It is applied after current year losses and before any transferred-in losses at the row below.
limitation: This column cannot be added to the collectables gains on the schedule: losses from collectables are ring-fenced, and the ATO warns that "If you have capital losses from collectables, you can only apply those to your capital gains from collectables." A high value also does not imply the entity was loss-making overall, only that it had stored capital losses and a gain to absorb them.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior year net capital losses applied row of the other capital gains column in part D of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions describe the choice of which gains to reduce and the collectables restriction.
evidence_quote: from any remaining capital gains in the way that produces the best result
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is where losses are worth the most.

value_domain: Capital losses transferred in applied, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 2C Applying net capital losses transferred
variable_description: Capital losses handed over by another company in the same wholly owned group and applied here against other-method gains. It is a narrow provision: "Transfer of net capital losses is only applicable to group companies", and one of the two companies must be "an Australian branch of a foreign bank" or an Australian permanent establishment of a foreign financial entity. Expect the column to be zero for almost every lodger.
value_definition: A dollar amount of losses received from a related company and used in this year against gains worked out under neither indexation nor the discount. It is applied at the third row of part D, after current year and prior year losses.
limitation: A non-zero value marks the entity as the receiving end of a group transfer, but nothing on the schedule identifies which company gave the losses up or what they cost. Read as a measure of the entity's own trading history it is misleading, because the losses were never made by this entity.
rationale: The DIL label names the capital losses transferred in applied row of the other capital gains column in part D of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions set out who may transfer a net capital loss and the Subdivision 170-B conditions.
evidence_quote: Transfer of net capital losses is only applicable to group companies.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the losses came from another company.

value_domain: Total capital losses applied, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part D label Q
variable_description: Every capital loss the entity applied against its indexation-method gains, added up. The form defines it arithmetically: "Add amounts at E to M above and write the total at Q below", which is the current year losses at E, the prior year losses at I and the transferred-in losses at M. It is the amount subtracted from the indexation column of total gains to reach part E.
value_definition: A dollar subtotal of the three loss rows in the indexation column of part D. It is a derived figure, so it duplicates amounts already reported in the same column rather than adding new information.
limitation: Adding this to the discount and other-method totals on the same row double counts nothing, but adding it to the individual loss rows above it does; treat it as a subtotal, not another loss. It also cannot show whether the losses were the entity's own or transferred from a group company, which only the rows above distinguish.
rationale: The DIL label names the total capital losses applied row of the indexation column in part D of the capital gains tax schedule, and the schedule form states the addition that produces it.
