The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au itself blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at E to M above and write the total at Q below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is a subtotal of the rows above it.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, indexation method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Indexation-method gains on assets outside the small business concessions, after capital losses have been taken off but before any concession. The non-active side of the schedule is the residual one: "If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets". Nothing further reduces this cell, because the CGT discount at part F applies only to the discount column.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of current year, prior year and transferred-in capital losses, and gross of the small business concessions. It is the top left cell of the part E grid.
limitation: The number is not the taxable gain even though nothing else reduces it in this column, because part G concessions and the part H subtraction still stand between it and the return. A zero can also mean losses exactly consumed the gains, which is a very different position from having made none.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active assets row of the indexation column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define what belongs on the non-active side.
evidence_quote: If the asset does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions, include the capital gain at Non-active assets
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which reductions had and had not been made at this point.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, discount method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 4 CGT discount on capital gains
variable_description: Discount-method gains on assets outside the small business concessions, after losses and immediately before the discount is worked out. This is the base the discount is calculated on, which is why the ATO applies losses first: at this part "you are calculating the amount of discount you can apply to reduce your capital gains after applying all losses". Half of this figure, or a third for a superannuation fund, becomes the discount reported at part F.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of all capital losses applied and gross of the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is the single most useful cell for reconstructing an entity's discountable gains.
limitation: It is not the amount that reaches assessable income; the discount at part F and any concessions at part G are subtracted afterwards. The discount rate that will be applied is not on the row either, and it differs between trusts and superannuation funds, so the taxable outcome cannot be derived without knowing the entity type.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active assets row of the discount column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions state that the discount is calculated on the gains remaining after all losses have been applied.
evidence_quote: you are calculating the amount of discount you can apply to reduce your capital gains after applying all losses
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this cell is the base the discount is worked out on.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, other method, non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Other-method gains on assets outside the small business concessions, after capital losses have been applied. For an entity claiming no concessions this is very close to the assessable gain, because neither the discount at part F nor the concessions at part G touch this column. The ATO directs a gain here whenever the asset "does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions" and neither indexation nor the discount was used.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of all capital losses applied. It is the third cell of the non-active row of part E and flows to the totals row below it.
limitation: For a company the column carries almost the whole capital gain rather than a short-held subset, so comparing companies with trusts on this cell alone compares tax rules rather than behaviour. It also cannot be split back into asset classes, which only part A holds.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-active assets row of the other capital gains column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the non-active side and the method columns.
evidence_quote: does not qualify for one or more of these 3 concessions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said how close this column is to the taxable amount.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, indexation method, active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Indexation-method gains on business assets that are heading for a small business concession, measured after capital losses. The ATO defines the class in ordinary terms: "Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business)." A gain only sits on the active side if the entity is actually claiming one of the three concessions on it, so this cell is the entry point to part G.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of all capital losses applied, measured against an indexed cost base, and gross of the small business concessions. It pairs with the non-active indexation cell directly above it in part E.
limitation: Whether an asset is active is a test the entity applies to itself, so the split records a claim rather than a verified fact. Gains covered by the small business 15 year exemption never appear here at all, being reported separately, so the active side understates business asset disposals by the longest held businesses.
rationale: The DIL label names the active assets row of the indexation column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define an active asset and restrict the active side to gains claiming one of the three concessions.
evidence_quote: Generally, an asset is an active asset if you use it, or hold it ready for use, in running a business (for example, goodwill of a business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing defined an active asset.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, discount method, active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Business asset gains held twelve months or more, after losses, and before both the CGT discount and the small business concessions. This is the cell that can be reduced twice over: the discount at part F halves it, then the fifty per cent active asset reduction at part G halves what is left. The ATO limits the active side to gains claiming one of the "small business 50% active asset reduction", the "small business retirement exemption" or the "small business roll-over".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of all capital losses applied and gross of every concession. It is the largest single input to a small business exit reported on this schedule.
limitation: It cannot be compared with the non-active discount cell as if the two faced the same tax: this one goes on to be reduced by concessions the other cannot claim. A business owner who used the 15 year exemption reports nothing here, so the column understates the value of businesses sold.
rationale: The DIL label names the active assets row of the discount column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions list the three concessions that qualify a gain for the active side.
evidence_quote: small business 50% active asset reduction
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this cell can be reduced twice.

value_domain: Current year capital gains after losses, other method, active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Step 2 active assets
variable_description: Business asset gains that get no discount and no indexation, after losses and before the small business concessions. A company selling business assets reports here rather than in the discount column, because it cannot use the discount. The ATO still requires the gain on the active side where the entity is claiming a concession, instructing that these gains be included "in the Active assets columns".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, net of all capital losses applied. Only the part G concessions stand between this cell and the net capital gain reported at part H.
limitation: A large value with nothing claimed at part G means the entity flagged assets as active and then took no concession, which is a lodgement inconsistency rather than a finding. The column also carries both quick disposals and long-held company assets, which have nothing else in common.
rationale: The DIL label names the active assets row of the other capital gains column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions require concession-eligible gains to be reported in the active assets columns.
evidence_quote: you must include in the Active assets columns capital gains for which your entity may be exempt
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which entities concentrate in this column.

value_domain: Total current year capital gains after losses, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part E label G
variable_description: All indexation-method gains left after capital losses, active and non-active together. The form states the arithmetic: "Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below." Part H then subtracts the concessions total from this figure to give the indexation share of the net capital gain, so G is the last unreduced total in this column.
value_definition: A dollar subtotal of the two rows above it in the indexation column of part E. It is derived, not separately reported, and equals total indexation gains less all indexation-column losses applied.
limitation: Because it merges the active and non-active rows, this total cannot say how much of the gain is eligible for a small business concession, which is exactly what the two rows above were split to show. It is also not comparable across the three method columns, since each column has been through a different set of reductions.
rationale: The DIL label names the totals row of the indexation column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the addition that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at A and D above and write the total at G below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is a derived subtotal.

value_domain: Total current year capital gains after losses, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part E label H
variable_description: All discount-method gains left after capital losses, and the base from which the CGT discount at part F is worked out. The form derives it as "Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below", that is the non-active and active discount cells. For a trust the discount reported in the next part will normally be half this number.
value_definition: A dollar subtotal of the two rows above it in the discount column of part E, net of every capital loss applied and gross of the discount and the concessions.
limitation: Halving it does not reproduce the taxable gain, because the small business concessions are applied afterwards and a superannuation fund discounts by a third rather than a half. Comparing it with the same entity's part A total also does not isolate losses, since losses were applied by column and could have been placed elsewhere.
rationale: The DIL label names the totals row of the discount column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the addition that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at B and E above and write the total at H below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing linked the total to the discount calculated in the next part.

value_domain: Total current year capital gains after losses, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part E label I
variable_description: All other-method gains left after capital losses, added across the active and non-active rows. The form sets it out as "Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below." No discount applies to this column, so for an entity claiming no small business concession this total is already the other-method share of the net capital gain.
value_definition: A dollar subtotal of the two rows above it in the other capital gains column of part E, net of every capital loss applied to that column.
limitation: This total looks small beside the discount-column total for a trust and large for a company, and that difference is the tax rules, not the size of the gains. It also hides the active and non-active split that determines whether concessions can be claimed at all.
rationale: The DIL label names the totals row of the other capital gains column in part E of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the addition that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at C and F above and write the total at I below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what the total contains or where it goes next.

value_domain: CGT discount applied to non-active assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Part 4 CGT discount on capital gains
variable_description: The dollar value of the CGT discount claimed on gains that are not business assets, mostly investment property and shares. The rate is not on the form and depends on the lodger: the ATO instructions set it at a third for a complying superannuation entity and a half for an individual or trust. A company reports nothing here, since "Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business."
value_definition: A dollar reduction, not a gain: it is the part of the discount-column gain removed by the discount. Its partner label covers active assets, and the two are added into the totals at part H.
limitation: Unlike the active asset label beside it, a gain discounted here can go no further, because the small business concessions at part G are closed to non-active assets. Dividing this figure by the gain does not reliably recover the discount rate either, because the rate follows the lodger rather than the asset: a half for a trust, a third for a complying superannuation entity.
rationale: The DIL label names the from non-active assets label in part F of the capital gains tax schedule, the part where the CGT discount is applied. The ATO instructions give the discount rates and the exclusion of companies.
evidence_quote: Companies are not eligible for the CGT discount unless they are life insurance companies or friendly societies that carry on life insurance business.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is a reduction rather than a gain, or which entities can claim it.

value_domain: Small business active asset reduction, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Small business CGT concessions
variable_description: The fifty per cent small business reduction claimed against business asset gains that were worked out under indexation. The ATO describes it simply: "The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset." In this column the reduction bites on the full indexed gain, because no CGT discount was taken first, unlike the discount-method label beside it.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain removed by the concession, not the gain itself. It sits with the retirement exemption and the roll-over as the three concessions claimable at part G.
limitation: The concession has eligibility conditions on turnover and net asset value that the entity tests for itself, so the column records a claim, not an entitlement. A zero here does not mean no concession was used, since the retirement exemption and the roll-over rows can carry the whole reduction instead.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business active asset reduction row of the indexation column in part G of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the concession.
evidence_quote: The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what the concession does or how the indexation column differs from the discount one.

value_domain: Small business retirement exemption, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Small business CGT concessions
variable_description: Business asset gains disregarded under the retirement exemption, where the gain was worked out by indexing the cost base. The ATO sets a lifetime cap and a condition on younger claimants: the exemption "allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000)", and "If you are eligible for this exemption and are under 55 years old just before you choose it, you must pay the amount into a superannuation (or similar) fund." It is the concession that turns a business sale into retirement savings.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain disregarded in this year under the exemption, in the indexation column of part G. It counts against a lifetime limit that this column, being one year of one entity, cannot show.
limitation: The amount is not a superannuation contribution, even though a claimant under 55 must make one: the contribution is reported through superannuation reporting, not here, and an older claimant need not contribute at all. The lifetime cap is also per individual, so an amount claimed by a company or trust cannot be attributed to one person from this row.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business retirement exemption row of the indexation column in part G of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the exemption, its lifetime limit and the contribution condition.
evidence_quote: The small business retirement exemption allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the eligibility conditions are satisfied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing mentioned the lifetime cap or the superannuation condition.

value_domain: Small business roll-over, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2024, Small business CGT concessions
variable_description: Business asset gains deferred rather than forgiven, on assets whose gain was worked out under indexation. The ATO frames it as a timing concession: the roll-over "enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions". A deferred gain comes back if the replacement asset is not acquired in time or is later sold.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain rolled over in this year, in the indexation column of part G. It reduces this year's net capital gain without extinguishing the liability.
limitation: Treating this as tax forgone overstates the concession, since the gain is only postponed and can reappear in a later year, which no column on this row records. Nothing here identifies the replacement asset, so the deferral cannot be tracked forward through the dataset.
rationale: The DIL label names the small business roll-over row of the indexation column in part G of the capital gains tax schedule. The ATO instructions define the roll-over as a deferral tied to a replacement asset.
evidence_quote: The small business roll-over enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the gain is deferred rather than removed.

value_domain: Total CGT discount and small business concessions, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part H label A
variable_description: Everything taken off the indexation column at parts F and G, added together. The form derives it as "Add amounts at L to R above and write the total at A below", which spans the active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over. Despite the row heading naming the CGT discount, no discount can appear in this column, because part F has boxes only in the discount column.
value_definition: A dollar subtotal of the three small business concession cells in the indexation column of part G. It is subtracted from the part E indexation total to give the indexation share of the net capital gain.
limitation: Reading it as a discount plus concessions figure, as the row heading invites, will misattribute the whole amount: in this column it is concessions only. It also cannot be compared with the discount-column total on the same row, which does include the discount and so measures something different.
rationale: The DIL label names the totals row of the indexation column in part H of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the addition that produces it and where the boxes for the CGT discount sit. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Add amounts at L to R above and write the total at A below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so the misleading row heading went unexplained.

value_domain: Net capital gain component, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part H label D
variable_description: The indexation-method share of the entity's assessable capital gain, after losses and concessions. The form works it out by subtraction: "Deduct the amount at A above from the amount at G in part E on page 2 and write the result at D below." With the discount and other-method shares it adds to the net capital gain that is transferred to the tax return.
value_definition: A dollar amount at the end of the calculation chain, net of every capital loss applied, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is one of three components that sum to the schedule's net capital gain.
limitation: It measures the gain on pre-September 1999 assets only, so a fall over time reflects those assets being sold off rather than any change in gains overall. It is a component, so adding it to the net capital gain column on the same record double counts.
rationale: The DIL label names the net capital gain row of the indexation column in part H of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the subtraction that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Deduct the amount at A above from the amount at G in part E on page 2 and write the result at D below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the figure is a component of the net capital gain.

value_domain: Net capital gain component, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part H label E
variable_description: The discounted share of the entity's assessable capital gain, and usually the largest of the three. The form derives it as "Deduct the amount at B above from the amount at H in part E on page 2 and write the result at E below", so the CGT discount and any small business concessions have already been removed. For a trust this is roughly half the discount-method gains that survived the loss step.
value_definition: A dollar amount net of all losses applied, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It is the discount-method component of the schedule's net capital gain.
limitation: It is a discounted figure, so it understates the economic gain by half for a trust and by a third for a superannuation fund; comparing it against an undiscounted amount elsewhere on the schedule mixes the two scales. A zero can also mean the discount and concessions between them removed the whole gain rather than that none was made.
rationale: The DIL label names the net capital gain row of the discount column in part H of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the subtraction that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Deduct the amount at B above from the amount at H in part E on page 2 and write the result at E below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount had already been discounted.

value_domain: Net capital gain component, other method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part H label F
variable_description: The undiscounted share of the entity's assessable capital gain, and for a company normally the whole of it. The form works the figure out as "Deduct the amount at C above from the amount at I in part E on page 2 and write the result at F below." Neither indexation nor the discount is available to a company, so its gains arrive here rather than in the two columns beside it. The three method components are added and the total transferred to the net capital gain label on the tax return.
value_definition: A dollar amount net of all losses applied and any small business concessions, with no discount taken off. It is the other-method component of the schedule's net capital gain.
limitation: Because no discount has been applied, this component is on a different scale from its discount-method neighbour, and summing entity types on it will overweight companies. It also cannot be traced back to an asset class, since part A holds that split and the method columns have been aggregated since part E.
rationale: The DIL label names the net capital gain row of the other capital gains column in part H of the capital gains tax schedule, and the form states the subtraction that produces it. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Deduct the amount at C above from the amount at I in part E on page 2 and write the result at F below.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule row label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this component carries no discount.

value_domain: Scrip for scrip roll-over chosen indicator (yes or no)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: Whether the entity chose to defer a takeover gain by taking shares instead of cash. The ATO describes the effect of choosing: "The rollover allows you to disregard the capital gain made from the original shares, units or other interest." The choice is only open where the takeover meets the conditions, and "A rollover does not apply to a capital loss."
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, not an amount. The 2001 edition of the schedule asks for Y or N and later editions for a cross in a Yes or No box, so the underlying code can differ between years.
limitation: A yes tells you a choice was made but not how much gain was deferred; that has to be inferred from the cost base and market value labels on the same row. A no does not mean the takeover was taxed, since the entity may simply not have been in a takeover that year.
rationale: The DIL label names label A in part K of the capital gains tax schedule, the scrip for scrip roll-over question for the exchanging taxpayer. The ATO guide explains what choosing the roll-over does.
evidence_quote: The rollover allows you to disregard the capital gain made from the original shares, units or other interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said what a scrip for scrip roll-over is or that the response is an indicator.

value_domain: Original interests cost base in a scrip for scrip roll-over (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: What the shares or units given up in a takeover had cost the entity, as reported by the shareholder side of the deal. This figure carries across to the new holding: "You are taken to have acquired the replacement shares, units or other interest for the cost base of the original interest." It is therefore the number that determines the tax on the eventual sale of the replacement shares, sometimes years later.
value_definition: A dollar cost base for the interests exchanged, not a gain or a sale price. Read with the replacement interests market value label beside it, the difference is the gain that the roll-over defers.
limitation: The cost base is not the market value of what was given up, so this column cannot value the takeover; the market value label on the same row does that. Where the entity received cash as well as shares only part of this cost base is rolled over, and the apportionment is not shown.
rationale: The DIL label names label B in part K of the capital gains tax schedule, the original interests cost base in a scrip for scrip roll-over. The ATO guide states that the replacement interest takes the cost base of the original interest.
evidence_quote: You are taken to have acquired the replacement shares, units or other interest for the cost base of the original interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the cost base carries forward to the replacement holding.

value_domain: Replacement interests market value in a scrip for scrip roll-over (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Takeovers and mergers
variable_description: What the new shares or units received in the takeover were worth when the entity got them. It is the value side of the exchange, against which the cost base of the original interests is measured. Where the conditions are not met the same value becomes taxable: "If the scrip for scrip conditions were not satisfied, your capital proceeds for your original shares is the total of any cash and of the market value of the new shares you received."
value_definition: A dollar market value measured at the time of the exchange, for the replacement interests only. It excludes any cash, which is reported at the cash and other considerations label on the same row.
limitation: This is a valuation at one moment, not a realised amount, and no tax is paid on it while the roll-over holds. It also does not tell you how many shares were received or in which company, so takeovers cannot be identified from this column alone.
rationale: The DIL label names label C in part K of the capital gains tax schedule, the replacement interests market value in a scrip for scrip roll-over. The ATO guide explains how market value of the new shares enters the calculation, though it defines the term in the context of a failed roll-over rather than for this label.
evidence_quote: If the scrip for scrip conditions were not satisfied, your capital proceeds for your original shares is the total of any cash and of the market value of the new shares you received.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which side of the exchange the value belongs to.

value_domain: Cash and other considerations received in a scrip for scrip roll-over (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: The cash or other non-share consideration the entity took in the takeover, which is the part that cannot be rolled over. The ATO explains why the label exists: "You may only be eligible for a partial rollover if you exchange shares, units or interests for similar interests in another entity (replacement interest) plus something else, usually cash." A non-zero amount here means a gain was taxed in the year of the takeover, not deferred.
value_definition: A dollar amount of consideration outside the roll-over, sitting beside the cost base and market value labels of part K. The cost base of the original interests has to be apportioned between it and the replacement interests.
limitation: The figure is proceeds, not gain: the taxable amount is this less the share of cost base allocated to it, which the schedule does not show. It also cannot be matched to the gain reported in part A, because that gain is reported by asset class rather than by transaction.
rationale: The DIL label names label D in part K of the capital gains tax schedule, cash and other considerations in a scrip for scrip roll-over. The ATO guide explains partial roll-over where cash is received alongside replacement interests.
evidence_quote: You may only be eligible for a partial rollover if you exchange shares, units or interests for similar interests in another entity (replacement interest) plus something else, usually cash.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said cash breaks the roll-over.

value_domain: Acquiring entity in a scrip for scrip roll-over indicator (yes or no)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: Whether the lodging entity is the takeover bidder rather than the shareholder being taken over. It flips the whole of part L from the target's point of view to the acquirer's, and the acquirer has to clear a control threshold for the roll-over to be available at all: "A rollover is only available if the exchange is in consequence of an arrangement that results in the acquiring entity (or the wholly owned group of which it is a member) becoming the owner of 80% or more of the original company or trust." The schedule restricts the part to companies and trusts.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, not an amount. It gates the remaining part L labels, which are only completed by an acquiring company or trust.
limitation: A yes identifies the entity as a bidder in the year, not the size or success of the bid, and it says nothing about the target beyond the count of original entities in the next label. Individuals never answer this question, so the column cannot be used to find takeovers involving unincorporated buyers.
rationale: The DIL label names label E in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the acquiring entity question. The ATO guide states the 80% ownership condition that defines an acquiring entity for the roll-over.
evidence_quote: A rollover is only available if the exchange is in consequence of an arrangement that results in the acquiring entity (or the wholly owned group of which it is a member) becoming the owner of 80% or more of the original company or trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the label marks the bidder side of a takeover.

value_domain: Count of original entities in a scrip for scrip roll-over
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part L label F
variable_description: How many target entities the acquirer took over under scrip for scrip arrangements in the year. It is a count, not a dollar figure, and it sits in the part of the schedule headed "Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity", which the form reserves for companies and trusts. The tax file number of the original entity is asked for on the same row, though that identifier is not carried into this dataset.
value_definition: A whole number of entities acquired, with no dollar units. It qualifies the cost base amounts reported at the other part L labels, which are totals across those entities.
limitation: The count says nothing about the size of the targets, so one large takeover and five small ones look alike. It also counts entities, not shareholders, so it cannot indicate how many holders took the roll-over.
rationale: The DIL label names label F in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the number of original entities, and the form shows the label as a count box rather than a dollar box. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Scrip-for-scrip rollover for acquiring entity
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the value is a count rather than an amount.

value_domain: Other considerations given by an acquiring entity (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: What the bidder handed over besides its own shares or units, usually cash, in a scrip for scrip takeover. It is the acquirer's record of the consideration that breaks the roll-over for the target holders, since "the rollover applies only to the replacement interest". Read with the number of original entities on the same row, it shows the cash component of the year's acquisitions.
value_definition: A dollar total of non-scrip consideration given, reported by the acquiring company or trust. It is the bidder-side counterpart of the cash and other considerations label in part K.
limitation: It is not the price of the takeover, because the shares issued as the main consideration are counted separately in the share and option counts, not in dollars. The two sides of the same deal also cannot be joined, as nothing here identifies the target holders.
rationale: The DIL label names label J in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the amount of other considerations given by the acquiring entity. The ATO guide explains why non-scrip consideration falls outside the roll-over.
evidence_quote: This is because the rollover applies only to the replacement interest.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said this is the bidder's non-scrip consideration.

value_domain: First element of cost base of interests acquired (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Cost base
variable_description: What the bidder records as the starting cost of the shares or units it acquired in the takeover. The first element is the narrowest part of a cost base: the ATO lists the five elements and puts first "money you paid, or property you gave, for the asset", with incidental and ownership costs following in the later elements. It fixes the acquirer's tax position on a later sale of the interests it has bought.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the first element only, so it excludes stamp duty, adviser fees and other incidental costs that belong to the second element. It is reported by the acquiring company or trust for the interests it acquired.
limitation: It is not the full cost base and should not be treated as the acquisition price of the target, which would also include the later elements. Where the target holders took the roll-over the acquirer's cost base can be capped by rules that look through to the target's own cost base, so the figure need not equal what was paid.
rationale: The DIL label names label K in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the first element of the cost base of interests acquired. The ATO definitions appendix sets out the five elements of a cost base and what the first element contains.
evidence_quote: The cost base of an asset is generally what the asset costs you. The cost base is made up of 5 elements:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing explained what a first element is or what it leaves out.

value_domain: Joint choice for scrip for scrip roll-over indicator (yes or no)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: Whether the bidder and a significant stakeholder in the target jointly chose the roll-over, a step required in closely held takeovers. The ATO flags the situation without naming the choice: "There are special rules if a company or trust has a small number of shareholders or beneficiaries and there is a significant or common stakeholder." Where those rules apply, the roll-over is not available on the target holder's election alone.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator, not an amount. It sits with the significant common stakeholder cost base label as the two part L items that deal with closely held targets.
limitation: The topic tag on this column reads superannuation in the source metadata, which is wrong; the label belongs to the scrip for scrip roll-over and has nothing to do with superannuation. A yes also does not identify the stakeholder or their holding, only that the joint choice was made.
rationale: The DIL label names label L in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the joint choice for roll-over question. The ATO guide describes the significant and common stakeholder rules that make a joint choice necessary, though it does not describe this label directly.
evidence_quote: There are special rules if a company or trust has a small number of shareholders or beneficiaries and there is a significant or common stakeholder.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and the superannuation topic tag was left unqualified.

value_domain: Cost base of significant common stakeholder interests acquired (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2021, Scrip for scrip rollover
variable_description: The cost base the bidder records for interests acquired from a significant or common stakeholder in a closely held takeover. It is reported separately because those stakeholders are the ones the anti-avoidance rules watch: "There are special rules if a company or trust has a small number of shareholders or beneficiaries and there is a significant or common stakeholder." In such cases the acquirer takes the stakeholder's own cost base rather than market value.
value_definition: A dollar cost base for one class of acquired interests, separate from the first element figure reported for the rest. It is completed only by an acquiring company or trust.
limitation: The label appears only where a stakeholder rule applies, so a zero usually means a widely held takeover rather than a cheap one. It also gives no count of the stakeholders or their share of the target, which cannot be recovered from anywhere else on the schedule.
rationale: The DIL label names label M in part L of the capital gains tax schedule, the cost base of significant common stakeholder interests acquired. The ATO guide describes the significant and common stakeholder rules that create this separate reporting, though it does not describe the label itself.
evidence_quote: There are special rules if a company or trust has a small number of shareholders or beneficiaries and there is a significant or common stakeholder.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said why stakeholder interests are reported apart.

value_domain: Employee share scheme in place indicator, companies only (yes or no)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), part M label N
variable_description: Whether the company ran an employee share scheme at any point in the year. The custodian's description, "To be completed by companies only", is the form's completion note rather than the question, which reads "Did you have an employee share scheme in place at any time during the year?" It is a standing yes or no about the company, not a CGT amount, and it sits in the schedule because share scheme interests generate CGT events for the employees who hold them.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator with no dollar value. The 2001 edition of the schedule asks for Y or N and later editions for a cross in a Yes or No box.
limitation: A yes says a scheme existed, not how many employees held interests, what they were worth, or whether any interests were issued that year. It is also answered only by companies, so an absent value on a trust or fund record is the form working as intended rather than a gap.
rationale: The DIL label names label N in part M of the capital gains tax schedule, which asks whether the company had an employee share scheme in place during the year and is restricted to companies. The ATO publication ordering service serves the form as a PDF; ato.gov.au blocks automated retrieval of the archived form.
evidence_quote: Did you have an employee share scheme in place at any time during the year?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the form's completion note, To be completed by companies only, as its whole description, so the page never stated the question being answered.

value_domain: Lodging entity type for the CGT schedule (company, trust or superannuation fund)
value_source: ATO, Capital gains tax (CGT) schedule 2010 (NAT 3423-6.2010), completion note
variable_description: Which kind of taxpayer lodged the schedule, and the column that decides how every dollar figure beside it should be read. The form is used "in conjunction with company, trust, fund income tax return or the self managed superannuation fund annual return", so those are the entities it covers. Entity type governs the tax rules: a company gets no CGT discount, a complying superannuation fund discounts by a third, and a trust by a half.
value_definition: A short entity type code, one value per record, running the full 2000-01 to 2022-23 span of the CGT product rather than only the years of the old long form.
limitation: The code list itself is not published in the source metadata, so the mapping from code to entity type has to be confirmed inside the DataLab before use. The column also describes the lodger, not the ultimate owner: a gain reported by a trust may be assessed to its beneficiaries, and nothing on this record says who they are.
rationale: The schedule form states which returns it accompanies, which bounds the set of entity types that can appear. No published page defines this particular column or its codes, so the reading of it as the lodging entity type is inferred from the variable name and from which returns carry the schedule.
evidence_quote: Use in conjunction with company, trust, fund income tax return or the self managed superannuation fund annual return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label Entity type as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said which entities lodge or why the distinction changes the numbers.

value_domain: Income year of the capital gains tax schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2025, Appendix 4 Definitions, Income year
variable_description: The tax year the schedule reports on, which is the year the CGT events happened rather than the year the return was lodged. The ATO defines it as "the period covered by your tax return, generally 1 July to the next 30 June", and adds that "in particular circumstances, the Commissioner may allow a company or other entity to adopt a different 12-month period for their income year". The CGT tables are already split one per income year, so this column repeats the table it sits in.
value_definition: A financial year identifier, one value per record, spanning 2000-01 to 2022-23 across the CGT product.
limitation: It is not a date of disposal: one row covers every CGT event in the year, so a gain cannot be placed within it. It is also not a lodgement date, and an entity with a substituted accounting period reports against a twelve-month window that does not run July to June, which makes an exact alignment with a calendar or Census year impossible.
rationale: The DIL label names the income year of the capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO definitions appendix defines an income year, including the substituted accounting period case.
evidence_quote: An income year is the period covered by your tax return, generally 1 July to the next 30 June.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word label Income year as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so nothing said the year is the year of the events, or that it can be a substituted period.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at label O, part N of the CGT schedule
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part N
variable_description: Whether the company still held assets bought before 20 September 1985 that Division 149 had not turned into post-CGT assets. The ATO puts the question as "At the end of the income year, did the company still have any assets that were acquired before 20 September 1985 and that were not treated as post-CGT assets under Division 149?" Division 149 resets the cost base of a pre-1985 asset once the majority underlying ownership of the company changes, so a yes marks a company still carrying genuinely grandfathered assets. Only companies answer it, which is why the custodian's wording is the eligibility line rather than the question.
value_definition: A single yes or no indicator at label O, with no dollar amount attached. Part N is answered by companies only, so trusts and funds leave it empty rather than answering no.
limitation: It cannot tell you how many pre-CGT assets there are or what they are worth, and a no is ambiguous: the company may never have held pre-1985 assets, or Division 149 may already have converted every one of them. The question was also reworded between years - by 2006 the ATO instead asked whether there had been no change in the majority underlying interests - so the same label does not carry the same question across the whole series.
rationale: The table cgt_2000_01 is the 2000-01 capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO's guide for that year gives the exact wording of part N and its single label O.
evidence_quote: At the end of the income year, did the company still have any assets that were acquired before 20 September 1985 and that were not treated as post-CGT assets under Division 149?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the eligibility line 'To be completed by companies only' as its whole description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which question the label answers.

value_domain: Cost base reduction after an intra-group debt forgiveness (dollars), label Q
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
variable_description: How much a company wrote off the cost base of its shares in, and loans to, an associated company after a debt inside the group was forgiven. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of all its shares and loans to the associated company", and only after the company answers yes at label P, which asks whether such a forgiveness or a substantial and permanent fall in the value of the debt happened. The amount matters because it lowers the gain the company can defer to a later year: value that left through the forgiven debt is taken out of the investment now.
value_definition: A dollar amount of cost base written off across all affected shares and loans, reported as one total rather than asset by asset. It is a reduction in the base of an unsold asset, so no capital gain or loss is recorded with it.
limitation: It does not record the debt that was forgiven, only the flow-on adjustment to the shareholder's cost bases, so it cannot be read as the size of the write-off inside the group. It is also separate from the Division 245 net forgiven amount that the debtor company applies against its own losses and cost bases, which this schedule never captures.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part O prefix with label Q, and the ATO's 2001 guide sets out part O of the schedule, its trigger question at label P and exactly what amount label Q carries.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label P is Y for yes, show at label Q the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of all its shares and loans to the associated company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base reduction' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell which of the schedule's two cost base reductions this was.

value_domain: Cost base adjustment on a CGT event after an earlier debt forgiveness (dollars), label S
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part O
variable_description: How much a company adjusted the cost base of its shares in an associated company when it later sold them, after a debt inside the group had been forgiven. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of all its shares in the associated company to which a CGT event happened", after a yes at label R. It is the later half of the same story as label Q on the same row: Q is the write-down when the debt goes, S is the correction made when the shares are finally disposed of.
value_definition: A dollar amount of adjustment reported as one total across the shares that a CGT event happened to. It covers shares only, not the loans that label Q also covers.
limitation: It records an adjustment made at disposal, so a company that took a forgiveness hit but held on to the shares reports nothing here even though its cost bases changed. A zero therefore cannot be read as no debt forgiveness in the group; label Q is the column that answers that.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part O prefix with label S, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part O in full, including the label R trigger question and the amount required at label S.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label R is Y for yes, show at label S the total amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of all its shares in the associated company to which a CGT event happened.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base adjustment' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it was indistinguishable from the loss transfer adjustment at label W.

value_domain: Count of options, rights or similar interests issued under a scrip for scrip arrangement, label I
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
variable_description: How many options, rights or similar interests the acquiring company or trust handed over in a scrip for scrip takeover. The ATO asks it of the acquirer: "Show at label I the number of options, rights or similar interests issued in exchange for the options, rights or similar interests acquired in the other entity." It sits beside the count of shares and units issued, so together the two columns describe the size of the paper consideration in a takeover where the target's holders took replacement scrip instead of cash.
value_definition: A whole number of instruments issued, not an amount of money. Only the acquiring entity completes it, and only after answering yes at label E to being an acquiring entity in a scrip for scrip arrangement.
limitation: A count of options and rights says nothing about their value, and options with different exercise prices are added together, so it cannot be scaled into consideration paid. Where the acquirer bought interests in several original entities it reports only the one arrangement with the greatest cost base, so the figure understates a multi-target year.
rationale: Part L of the CGT schedule has labels E to M, and the registry holds a variable for every one of them except the target's tax file number at G and the two counts at H and I; this column is the options and rights count that the ATO requires at label I.
evidence_quote: Show at label I the number of options, rights or similar interests issued in exchange for the options, rights or similar interests acquired in the other entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text 'Number of options/rights etc issued' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say that the count belongs to a scrip for scrip takeover or who reports it.

value_domain: Cost base adjustment where a group company received a transferred loss (dollars), label W
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
variable_description: The cost base adjustment a company made on selling shares in a group company that had earlier been given a tax loss by another member of the group. The ATO asks for "the amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of such assets" once label V is answered yes. Receiving a loss makes the subsidiary worth more, so the adjustment runs the opposite way to the reduction at label U on the same row, where the subsidiary had given a loss away.
value_definition: A dollar amount of adjustment, totalled across the shares and loans that a CGT event happened to in the year. Part P is answered by companies only.
limitation: The direction of the adjustment is not recorded, so the column cannot be added to the reduction at label U to get a net figure without assuming which way each ran. Nothing here identifies the group company that transferred the loss or the size of the loss itself.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part P prefix with label W, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part P in full, including the label V question about losses transferred into the investee and the amount required at label W.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label V is Y for yes, show at label W the amount by which the company adjusted the cost bases of such assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base adjustment', identical to the debt forgiveness label, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Cost base reduction where a group company transferred a loss away (dollars), label U
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part P
variable_description: The cost base write-down a company made on selling shares in a group company that had earlier handed a tax loss to another member of the group. The ATO asks for "the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of such assets" once label T is answered yes. A company that gives away a loss gives away future deductions, so the investment in it is worth less and the holder must take that value out of its cost base rather than bank it as a capital loss on sale.
value_definition: A dollar amount of cost base removed, totalled across the shares and loans that a CGT event happened to in the year. Part P is answered by companies only.
limitation: It measures the adjustment, not the loss transferred, so it cannot be used to size loss trading inside a group. Only assets that a CGT event happened to in the year appear, so a group that transfers losses freely but never sells the underlying shares reports nothing.
rationale: The DIL label pairs the part P prefix with label U, and the ATO's 2001 guide gives part P in full, including the label T question about a loss transferred out of the investee and the amount required at label U.
evidence_quote: If the answer at label T is Y for yes, show at label U the total amount by which the company reduced the cost bases of such assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare label text 'Total Cost base reduction', identical to the debt forgiveness label, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Count of shares, units or other interests issued under a scrip for scrip arrangement, label H
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), part C, instructions to complete the CGT schedule, part L
variable_description: How many shares, units or other interests the acquiring company or trust issued to the target's holders in a scrip for scrip takeover. The ATO asks it of the acquirer: "Show at label H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity." Scrip for scrip roll-over lets the target's holders defer their capital gain because they were paid in paper, so this count is the volume of that paper, with the cost base of the interests acquired reported separately at label K.
value_definition: A whole number of shares, units or other interests issued, not an amount of money. Only the acquiring entity completes it, and only after answering yes at label E.
limitation: A share count cannot be turned into value without a price, and shares of different classes are added together, so it is not a measure of the deal size. It is also reported only for the single arrangement with the greatest cost base where several targets were acquired in the year.
rationale: Part L of the CGT schedule has labels E to M, and the registry holds a variable for every one of them except the target's tax file number at G and the two counts at H and I; this column is the shares and units count that the ATO requires at label H.
evidence_quote: Show at label H the number of shares, units or other interests issued in exchange for the shares or units or other interests acquired in the original entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label text 'Number of shares/units etc. issued' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing connected the count to a takeover or said who reports it.

value_domain: Small business active asset reduction, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The whole-of-year small business 50% active asset reduction, reported as one figure rather than split by calculation method. The ATO describes the concession plainly: "The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset." It is the redesigned schedule's version of the same claim that the older schedule carried in three method columns, and in this registry those method columns stop after the first 2012-13 file while this column runs across all twenty-four year tables.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain removed by the concession, taken after losses and the CGT discount and before the net capital gain. It sits at item 5 label A with the retirement exemption and the roll-over at labels B and C.
limitation: Because the older schedule split the same claim three ways, a series that reads this column alone breaks at the schedule change and has to be rebuilt by adding the indexation, discount and other-method columns for the early years. Eligibility is self-assessed against turnover and net asset value tests, so the column records a claim rather than a verified entitlement.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the concession and place it at item 5, and the registry's own table lists show the split-by-method labels ending after cgt_2012_13_part1 while this column continues to 2022-23.
evidence_quote: The small business 50% active asset reduction provides a 50% reduction of a capital gain for an active asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business active asset reduction' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that an earlier schedule reported the same claim in three separate columns.

value_domain: Total small business concessions applied (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: Three of the four small business concessions added together at item 5 label D: the 50% active asset reduction, the retirement exemption and the roll-over. The fourth concession is deliberately outside it, because the ATO says this part "doesn't include the small business 15-year exemption which is shown separately at item 8 of the CGT schedule". A gain fully wiped out by the 15-year exemption never enters the schedule's arithmetic at all, so this column understates total small business relief by exactly the largest concession of the four.
value_definition: A dollar amount that is the sum of the three concession columns beside it, applied after the CGT discount and before the net capital gain. Adding it to those three columns double-counts.
limitation: It treats a roll-over, which only defers tax, as equivalent to an exemption, which forgives it, so it overstates the revenue given up in the year by whatever share was deferred. It also omits the 15-year exemption entirely, which sits at item 8 and is the concession that disregards a gain in full.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define item 5 as the sum of labels A, B and C at label D, and state that the 15-year exemption is reported separately at item 8.
evidence_quote: This part doesn't include the small business 15-year exemption which is shown separately at item 8 of the CGT schedule (if a schedule is required).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Total small business concessions applied' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the exclusion of the 15-year exemption was nowhere on the page.

value_domain: Small business roll-over, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The gain a small business put off rather than gave up, by buying a replacement asset or improving one it already had. The ATO defines the concession as one that "enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions". On a business file a figure here reads as reinvestment, which is the opposite signal to the retirement exemption in the column beside it, where the owner is taking money out.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain deferred, not forgiven, reported at item 5 label C without a split by calculation method. Nothing in this dataset records the year in which a deferred gain is brought back to account.
limitation: Treating the amount as tax relief overstates the concession, because a roll-over is a timing difference that resurfaces when the replacement asset goes or the conditions fail. The replacement asset test is applied by the taxpayer after the fact, so a claim can be unwound in a later amendment that this column will not show.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the small business roll-over and place it at item 5 label C alongside the other two concessions.
evidence_quote: The small business roll-over enables you to defer all or part of a capital gain if you acquire a replacement asset or make an improvement to an existing asset and satisfy other conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business roll-over' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a deferral from an exemption.

value_domain: Small business retirement exemption, all calculation methods (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 5
variable_description: The gain a small business owner disregarded under the retirement exemption, which is capped over a lifetime rather than a year. The ATO says it "allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the eligibility conditions are satisfied". A claimant under 55 must pay the amount into superannuation, so a figure here should have a matching contribution in the superannuation records elsewhere in the asset. The lifetime cap is what makes a single year's figure hard to read on its own.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain disregarded, at item 5 label B, with no split by calculation method. It counts toward a lifetime limit, and the running total a person has used is held nowhere in this dataset.
limitation: One year's claim cannot be interpreted without the claimant's history, and where a company or trust makes the claim the lifetime limit attaches to the individual behind it rather than the lodging entity, so the file cannot show whether the cap was reached. Eligibility is self-assessed.
rationale: The ATO's current schedule instructions define the retirement exemption, state the lifetime limit and the superannuation condition, and place the claim at item 5 label B.
evidence_quote: The small business retirement exemption allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the eligibility conditions are satisfied.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label 'Small business retirement exemption' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the lifetime cap was not stated anywhere on the page.

value_domain: Seller's estimated total capital proceeds from an earnout arrangement (dollars), item 7 label D
value_source: ATO, Instructions to complete the CGT schedule and tax return 2025, item 7 Earnout arrangements
variable_description: What a seller expects to end up with in total from a business sale whose price depends on how the business performs after the handover. The ATO's instruction is short - "Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement" - but the surrounding rule is what matters: a seller completes labels D and E only "for arrangements which don't involve look-through earnout rights". Since look-through treatment covers rights created on or after 24 April 2015, this column captures the shrinking remainder of arrangements outside that treatment.
value_definition: A dollar estimate of proceeds across the whole arrangement, not the year, made by the seller at lodgment. Labels B and C beside it give the arrangement's length in years and the year the seller is in.
limitation: It is a forecast, not a settled amount, so it cannot be reconciled with what the seller actually received; the realised gain or loss for the year sits in a separate column. A blank does not mean no earnout, because sellers under a look-through right leave it empty by instruction, and buyers never complete it at all.
rationale: The custodian's description is the schedule's own question wording, and the ATO's current schedule instructions give item 7 label D, who completes it and the look-through exclusion that governs when it is left blank.
evidence_quote: Write at label D the total estimated capital proceeds from the earnout arrangement.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule question as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the figure is an estimate or that look-through arrangements are excluded.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person a capital gains tax schedule row is attached to, and the key that carries an asset disposal out to their other records in PLIDA. ABS keeps the joining information away from the data itself: the "Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data". Read this column with ENTITY_TYPE and BN on the same row, because a CGT schedule is lodged by a taxpaying entity, and a person-level count of gains that ignores the entity type will mix individuals with the companies, trusts and funds beside them.
value_definition: An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, stable across every column of the row and across the twenty-four year tables. In fplida the values are generated rather than derived from anyone.
limitation: It identifies a person, not a taxpaying entity, a household or a business, so it cannot answer who controls a company that lodged a schedule. Only entities with more than $10,000 of gains or losses must lodge, so a person with no row in a year is not a person with no capital gains.
rationale: ABS describes the PLIDA spine and how linkage keys are held separately from the data, which is what this column is; the surrounding CGT columns show it is carried alongside an entity type and a business number rather than on its own.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the row belongs to a lodging entity as well as a person.

value_domain: Capital gains amount, indexation method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2001 (NAT 4151), the indexation method
variable_description: Total capital gains for the year worked out by inflating the cost base rather than halving the gain, which only assets bought before the 1999 reform can use. The ATO limits it to a CGT event on "an asset you acquired before 11.45am on 21 September 1999" that was held for twelve months or more, and the indexation itself stops early: "As indexation is frozen as at 30 September 1999, you can index your cost base only up to the September 1999 quarter." Read against the discount-method and other-method totals on the same row, this column marks the disposal of assets held since the old regime.
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of capital losses and of the small business concessions. No further discount is applied to these gains, because the inflation relief has already been taken inside the cost base.
limitation: The column can only shrink over time, since no asset acquired after September 1999 can ever enter it, so a fall across years is a change in the eligible stock rather than in behaviour. In this registry it stops after the first 2012-13 file, when the schedule dropped the method split, so a series that continues past that point is not the same measure.
rationale: The DIL label names the total current year capital gains under the indexation method, a defined column of the 2000-01 capital gains tax schedule, and the ATO's guide for that year sets out when the method is available and how far indexation runs.
evidence_quote: As indexation is frozen as at 30 September 1999, you can index your cost base only up to the September 1999 quarter.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the schedule label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why a third method column exists or why it empties out over time.

value_domain: ATO processing date
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day the ATO put this capital gains tax schedule through its systems, which is an administrative date rather than anything about the assets. It is the only date on the row: the income year the figures belong to is carried by INCM_YR, and no column records when a CGT event actually happened. Its practical use is vintage, telling you how long after the end of an income year a record was settled, and how far apart two rows for the same year were processed.
value_definition: A calendar date. The domain is open, running from the earliest processing in the series to the extract date rather than being confined to the income year on the row.
limitation: It is not the lodgment date and not the date of any disposal, so a gain cannot be timed from it; a schedule processed in one year routinely reports events from an earlier one. An amended schedule is processed again, so where amendments survive as their own rows the column dates the amendment rather than the original claim.
rationale: No published ATO page defines this field. The reading comes from the custodian's wording, from the column sitting alone as the only date beside INCM_YR, and from the general PLIDA description of the tax records as ATO administrative extracts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Processed date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned a reader against using it to date a capital gain.
